# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jul 15, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing Superchain interoperability with new Super-range and Super-root features, alongside significant documentation improvements and critical bug fixes.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Superchain Interoperability and Fault Proofs
Significant progress was made in advancing Superchain interoperability and fault proof mechanisms. New features include the execution of Super-range consolidation proofs ([#21677](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21677)) and Super-range range proofs ([#21671](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21671)) within the Kona SP1 guest. Support for Super-root fault games at initial deployment was also added ([#21720](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21720)), ensuring game types align with the `SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION`. Testing efforts included preparing and using production Super-root proposal sources in e2e tests ([#21742](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21742), [#21738](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21738)) and validating ZK after Super-root migration ([#21771](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21771)).

### Core Client Consistency and Bug Fixes
Improvements were made to ensure consistency across OP Stack clients and address critical bugs. The operator opt-in flag for SDM PostExec was standardized across clients ([#21551](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21551)). A bug in `op-acceptance-tests` that incorrectly set fork schedules was fixed ([#21642](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21642)). The `op-reth` client was updated to include a fix for `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` ([#21766](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21766)), and three unauthenticated attack surfaces in the Kona client were closed ([#21753](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21753)). Additionally, the batch upgrade test was made `SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION`-aware ([#21803](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21803)).

### Documentation Restructuring and Enhancements
Extensive work was done to improve the organization and clarity of the documentation. This included moving the chain-operator network design example from reference to guides ([#21770](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21770)), surfacing node system requirements on the node-operator overview ([#21761](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21761)), and adding a snapshot restore how-to guide for node operators ([#21819](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21819)). Several pages were split by mode (e.g., app-developer standard-bridge and integrating-wallets ([#21818](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21818)), governance FAQ ([#21817](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21817)), Kona pages ([#21816](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21816)), node-operator supernode and legacy-geth ([#21815](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21815)), flashblocks ([#21814](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21814)), batcher configuration ([#21813](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21813)), op-deployer releases ([#21812](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21812)), and op-conductor ([#21796](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21796))) to improve user experience. Dead-end and chained legacy redirects were also fixed ([#21781](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21781)).
